Spacing Demos

Spacing is token-only — card-style tokens embedded in the breakpoint attributes (there are no bare pad-*/col-gap attributes). Tokens use a multiplier applied to --layout-space-unit. The lowest breakpoint (xs, un-media-queried) is the mobile-first base that applies at all widths; larger breakpoints override it. Resize the viewport to see the overrides.

Steps come in two spellings, both multipliers of --layout-space-unit: numbers (cg(0)–cg(4)) and word sizes following the content-DSL ladder — 2xs 0.125 · xs 0.25 · sm 0.5 · md 1 · lg 1.5 · xl 2 · 2xl 3. At the default 1rem unit that makes cg(2xs) a 2px hairline and cg(xs) 4px.

Note: this build generates spacing tokens for the xs and lg breakpoints (the spacing.breakpoints allowlist in layout.config.json) — xs is the mobile-first base. Add breakpoints to the allowlist (e.g. xl for mosaic tiers) to author spacing there too.

All-sides padding — p()

Base padding p(1) on all sides (from 0px up), growing to p(4) at lg.

<lay-out xs="columns(2) p(1)" lg="columns(4) p(4)">

Padding-inline & padding-block — pi() / pb()

Inline padding grows from pi(1) (base) to pi(4) at lg; block padding pb() sets top + bottom together.

<lay-out xs="columns(2) pi(1) pb(1)" lg="columns(4) pi(4) pb(2)">

Asymmetric block padding — pbs() / pbe()

Block-start (pbs) and block-end (pbe) set independently — here more padding at the bottom.

<lay-out xs="columns(2) pbs(1) pbe(2)" lg="columns(3) pbs(2) pbe(4)">

Margin spacing (block only) — mbs() / mbe()

Vertical separation between layouts using mbe (margin-block-end). The gap below the first grid grows at lg. (Margin is block-only — margin-inline stays auto for centering.)

<lay-out xs="columns(2) pb(1) mbe(2)" lg="columns(2) pb(2) mbe(4)">

Gap control — cg() / rg()

Column gap and row gap controlled independently. Small gaps at the base, wider at lg.

<lay-out xs="columns(2) cg(1) rg(1)" lg="columns(3) cg(2) rg(3)">

Zero gaps — removing all spacing between items.

<lay-out xs="columns(3) cg(0) rg(0)" lg="columns(4) cg(0) rg(0)">

Word sizes — cg(2xs) … p(2xl)

The word ladder on gaps: 2xs (2px) at the base, sm (8px) at lg. Words and numbers mix freely.

<lay-out xs="columns(3) cg(2xs) rg(2xs)" lg="columns(3) cg(sm) rg(sm)">

Hairlines — background color through tiny gaps

A 2px gap (cg(2xs) / rg(2xs)) with matching padding (p(2xs)) lets --layout-bg read as hairlines between items — the mosaic-lines look. (For rules inside larger gaps, see the companion gap-decorations attribute.)

<lay-out xs="columns(2) cg(2xs) rg(2xs) p(2xs)" lg="grid(3c) cg(2xs) rg(2xs) p(2xs)">

Per-breakpoint gap change

Allowlisted breakpoints can each set their own gap: xs (8px base) → lg (2px hairline with the pattern switch). Resize to watch the gap change with the layout.

<lay-out xs="columns(2) cg(sm) rg(sm)" lg="grid(3a) cg(2xs) rg(2xs)">

Combined tokens

Multiple spacing tokens in a single attribute — padding, gaps and margin, all set at the base and overridden at lg.

<lay-out xs="columns(2) pi(1) pb(1) cg(1) rg(1)" lg="columns(3) pi(3) pb(2) cg(2) rg(2)">

Base (xs) + breakpoint override

The xs tokens are the mobile-first base — they apply at all widths because xs has no media query. At lg, the pi(3) token overrides pi(1).

<lay-out xs="columns(2) pi(1) pb(1)" lg="columns(3) pi(3) pb(2)">

Grid layout with spacing

A grid layout pattern with responsive spacing — compact at the base, spacious at lg.

<lay-out xs="grid(3a) pi(1) pb(1) cg(1)" lg="grid(3a) pi(3) pb(2) cg(2) rg(2)">
